AI/ML Engineer.title: AI/ML Engineer
AI/ML Engineer.description: Designs, develops, and deploys scalable machine learning models and deep learning architectures to solve complex real-world predictive and generative problems.
career_progression: Senior ML Engineer / Lead AI Engineer
Staff AI Scientist / Head of AI
interview_tips: Master mathematical intuition behind algorithms (gradient descent, loss functions, backpropagation).
Be prepared to code ML algorithms from scratch and explain bias-variance trade-offs.
Practice system design for ML (data ingestion, feature store, latency constraints, model monitoring).
interview_questions: Explain the difference between L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) regularization and when to use which.
How do Transformer attention mechanisms differ from traditional RNNs and LSTMs?
How would you address severe class imbalance in a fraud detection dataset?
Explain vanishing and exploding gradients and how modern architectures mitigate them.
learning_roadmap: Phase 1 (Foundations): Linear Algebra, Multivariable Calculus, Probability, Advanced Python, OOP, NumPy, Pandas.
Phase 2 (Classical ML): Regression, Decision Trees, Ensembles (XGBoost/LightGBM), Scikit-learn, Feature Engineering.
Phase 3 (Deep Learning & NLP/CV): Neural Networks, CNNs, Transformers, PyTorch/TensorFlow, Fine-tuning LLMs.
Phase 4 (Production & MLOps): Model Serving (FastAPI/Triton), Docker, CI/CD for ML, Drift Detection, MLflow.

Data Scientist.title: Data Scientist
Data Scientist.description: Extracts actionable insights from structured and unstructured data using exploratory analysis, statistical hypothesis testing, and predictive modeling.
career_progression: Principal Data Scientist / Director of Data Science
interview_tips: Focus deeply on A/B testing design, p-values, hypothesis framing, and business metric impact.
Demonstrate structured business thinking: translate vague business problems into quantifiable ML formulations.
Be confident in complex SQL window functions, joins, and aggregations.
interview_questions: How do you design an A/B test for a new checkout recommendation feature?
What metrics would you use to evaluate an imbalanced classification problem?
Explain the Central Limit Theorem and its significance in statistical inference.
How do you detect and handle multicollinearity in regression models?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Statistics & Probability, Python Data Stack (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn), Advanced SQL.
Phase 2: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), Hypothesis Testing, Feature Selection, Supervised & Unsupervised Learning.
Phase 3: Big Data processing with PySpark, Experimentation (A/B testing), Dashboarding (Tableau/Power BI).
Phase 4: Advanced Predictive Modeling, Business Communication, Cloud Data Warehouses (BigQuery/Snowflake).

Data Analyst.title: Data Analyst
Data Analyst.description: Translates raw corporate data into interactive dashboards, KPI reports, and strategic intelligence to guide daily and long-term executive decisions.
career_progression: Analytics Manager / VP of Business Intelligence
interview_tips: Master complex SQL queries (Window functions like RANK, DENSE_RANK, LEAD, LAG, CTEs).
Prepare a portfolio of interactive dashboards showcasing clear narrative hierarchy and business impact.
Understand key business metrics (CAC, LTV, Churn, ROI, Conversion Funnel).
interview_questions: Write a SQL query using CTE and Window functions to find the top 3 highest spending customers per region.
What is the difference between a Star Schema and a Snowflake Schema in data modeling?
How do you choose between a bar chart, line chart, scatter plot, and treemap?
How would you investigate a sudden 20% drop in active users over the weekend?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Advanced Excel (VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, Pivot Tables, Power Query), Relational Database Concepts.
Phase 2: In-depth SQL (joins, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, query optimization).
Phase 3: BI Tools (Power BI or Tableau) including data modeling, calculated measures, and UX.
Phase 4: Python for analytics (Pandas, automated reporting) and exploratory statistical analysis.

Software Engineer.title: Software Engineer
Software Engineer.description: Architects, writes, and tests robust, modular software code and backend systems with high performance, scalability, and maintainability.
interview_tips: Practice Data Structures & Algorithms on LeetCode (Trees, Graphs, Dynamic Programming, HashMaps).
Master High-Level and Low-Level System Design (caching, database sharding, microservices, load balancing).
Know clean code principles (SOLID, DRY, Design Patterns) and debugging techniques.
interview_questions: How would you design a distributed URL shortening service like TinyURL?
Explain how a Hash Table handles hash collisions (Chaining vs Open Addressing).
Explain the differences between optimistic locking and pessimistic locking.
What are the ACID properties in database transactions and how is isolation implemented?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Master one language (Java/C++/Python/Go), OOP fundamentals, Memory Management, Linux CLI.
Phase 2: Data Structures & Algorithms (Arrays, Linked Lists, Trees, Graphs, Sorting, DP).
Phase 3: Database design, REST APIs, Multithreading, Concurrency, Unit Testing & Git.
Phase 4: Distributed Systems, Microservices, Caching (Redis), Message Queues (Kafka/RabbitMQ), System Design.

Full Stack Developer.title: Full Stack Developer
Full Stack Developer.description: Builds end-to-end web applications, designing interactive client-side interfaces and scalable server-side APIs and database architectures.
career_progression: Senior Full Stack Engineer / Tech Lead
interview_tips: Build and showcase 2-3 full-stack applications with authentication, state management, and real databases.
Understand browser fundamentals: Event Loop, DOM rendering, CORS, WebSockets, and caching.
Be prepared to code full CRUD endpoints and interactive UI components in live coding rounds.
interview_questions: Explain the JavaScript Event Loop, microtasks, and macrotasks.
How does React's Virtual DOM reconciliation and Fiber architecture work?
How do you implement secure user authentication using JWT and Refresh Tokens?
Compare SQL (PostgreSQL) vs NoSQL (MongoDB) for an e-commerce catalog.
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: HTML5 semantic tags, Modern CSS (Flexbox, Grid, Responsive), JavaScript ES6+ fundamentals.
Phase 2: Frontend Frameworks (React, State Management with Redux/Zustand, Tailwind CSS).
Phase 3: Backend Development (Node.js/Express or Python/FastAPI), RESTful API design, SQL & NoSQL.
Phase 4: Full-Stack Frameworks (Next.js), Authentication (OAuth/JWT), Dockerization, Cloud Deployment (Vercel/AWS).

DevOps & Cloud Engineer.title: DevOps & Cloud Engineer
DevOps & Cloud Engineer.description: Bridges software development and IT operations through automated CI/CD pipelines, containerization, Infrastructure as Code, and resilient cloud architectures.
career_progression: Head of Infrastructure / VP of Cloud Operations
interview_tips: Understand Kubernetes architecture (Control Plane, Worker Nodes, Pods, Services, Ingress, Deployments).
Write modular Terraform scripts demonstrating state management, modules, and multi-environment setups.
Understand observability principles: Metrics, Logs, Traces (Prometheus, ELK/OpenTelemetry, Grafana).
interview_questions: Explain the pod lifecycle in Kubernetes and how a Rolling Update deployment works.
How do you manage Terraform remote state file locking and secrets management?
What is the difference between Blue-Green and Canary deployment strategies?
How would you troubleshoot high CPU utilization or an OOMKilled container in production?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Linux fundamentals, Bash/Python scripting, Networking (DNS, TCP/IP, SSL/TLS, SSH).
Phase 2: Version control (Git), Containerization with Docker, CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions/Jenkins).
Phase 3: Public Cloud core services (AWS/GCP/Azure: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, CloudWatch).
Phase 4: Container orchestration (Kubernetes), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), Monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana).

Cyber Security Engineer.title: Cyber Security Engineer
Cyber Security Engineer.description: Protects digital assets, networks, and applications from vulnerabilities, unauthorized intrusion, ransomware, and state-sponsored cyber attacks.
career_progression: Senior Security Architect / Red Team Lead
interview_tips: Deeply study OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (SQLi, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, Broken Access Control) and remedies.
Understand OSI Model packet inspection and secure network architecture (Firewalls, DMZ, Zero Trust).
Obtain or study industry certifications like CompTIA Security+, CEH, or OSCP.
interview_questions: Explain the difference between Symmetric and Asymmetric encryption and how TLS/SSL handshake operates.
How does a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack work, and how can applications prevent it?
What is Zero Trust architecture and how does it challenge traditional perimeter security?
Explain the steps involved in incident response during a suspected ransomware outbreak.
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Computer Networking (OSI model, TCP/IP, DNS, Routing), Linux and Windows system internals.
Phase 2: Security fundamentals, Cryptography (Hashing, Ciphers, PKI), Web Application Security (OWASP Top 10).
Phase 3: Ethical Hacking tools (Nmap, Burp Suite, Wireshark, Metasploit), SOC operations & SIEM (Splunk).
Phase 4: Advanced Threat Hunting, Cloud Security (AWS/Azure IAM & GuardDuty), Penetration Testing methodologies.

Cloud Solutions Architect.title: Cloud Solutions Architect
Cloud Solutions Architect.description: Designs robust, secure, resilient, and cost-effective enterprise cloud architectures aligned with business goals and compliance mandates.
interview_tips: Master the AWS/Azure Well-Architected Framework (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance, Cost Optimization).
Demonstrate cloud migration strategies (The 6 R's: Rehost, Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Retire, Retain).
Practice whiteboard architecture scenarios balancing throughput, failover, and budgetary constraints.
interview_questions: How do you design a multi-region active-active database failover system with sub-second RPO and RTO?
Explain the trade-offs between Serverless compute and Containerized microservices on Kubernetes.
How would you reduce an enterprise AWS bill by 35% without degrading performance?
Design a secure hybrid-cloud network connection connecting on-premises data centers to AWS VPC.
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Cloud fundamentals (Compute, Storage, Networking, IAM on AWS/GCP/Azure).
Phase 2: High availability, load balancing, auto-scaling, relational vs NoSQL cloud databases.
Phase 3: Microservices, serverless computing, event-driven architectures, Infrastructure as Code.
Phase 4: Well-Architected Framework, multi-region disaster recovery, enterprise security, FinOps cost optimization.

Product Manager.title: Product Manager
Product Manager.description: Drives the product vision, roadmap, and execution at the intersection of business, technology, and user experience, delivering customer value.
career_progression: VP of Product / Chief Product Officer (CPO)
interview_tips: Structure product design answers using CIRCLES framework (Comprehend, Identify, Report, Cut, Explore, List, Evaluate, Summarize).
Back every argument with measurable metrics (North Star metric, retention cohorts, conversion rates).
Demonstrate empathy for engineering constraints and UX principles.
interview_questions: How would you improve Google Maps for senior citizens?
Pick your favorite mobile app. What feature would you deprecate and why?
If you notice an e-commerce cart abandonment spike of 15% this morning, what steps do you take?
How do you prioritize competing feature requests from Sales, Engineering, and Executive Leadership?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Product lifecycle fundamentals, Agile methodologies (Scrum/Kanban), User Story mapping.
Phase 2: Quantitative analytics (SQL, Product Analytics with Mixpanel/Amplitude, A/B testing).
Phase 3: User research, Wireframing (Figma), PRD (Product Requirements Document) writing.
Phase 4: Product Strategy, Go-To-Market (GTM) execution, Pricing strategy, Executive presentation.

Mobile Application Developer.title: Mobile Application Developer
Mobile Application Developer.description: Creates intuitive, high-performance mobile applications for Android and iOS operating systems with smooth animations and native hardware integration.
interview_tips: Showcase a published app on Google Play Store or Apple App Store.
Master state management paradigms (Bloc, Provider, Riverpod, Redux).
Understand offline-first caching, background services, push notifications, and battery optimization.
interview_questions: What is the difference between Flutter (Canvas rendering) and React Native (Bridge/JSI)?
How do you optimize an app for 60/120 FPS scrolling and avoid UI jank?
Explain the Android Activity/Fragment lifecycle or iOS ViewController lifecycle.
How does offline data synchronization work with local SQLite/Hive and remote cloud databases?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Programming mastery (Dart for Flutter, or Kotlin/Swift for Native development).
Phase 2: Mobile UI components, responsive widget layout, user input handling, animations.
Phase 3: State management, network HTTP calls, local storage (SQLite, SharedPreferences), Firebase auth.
Phase 4: App profiling, memory leak detection, CI/CD with Fastlane, App Store publishing.

UI/UX Designer.title: UI/UX Designer
UI/UX Designer.description: Crafts beautiful, accessible, human-centered digital experiences through extensive user research, wireframing, interactive prototyping, and design systems.
career_progression: Head of Design / VP of User Experience
interview_tips: Present a portfolio showcasing end-to-end case studies from problem statement to user feedback.
Articulate the 'Why' behind every design decision rather than just aesthetics.
Understand Web Accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA, contrast ratios, keyboard navigation).
interview_questions: Walk me through your design process when starting a brand new project from scratch.
How do you resolve disagreements with engineers regarding feasibility of complex UI animations?
What is the difference between quantitative and qualitative user research?
How do you maintain consistency using scalable Design Systems and atomic design?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Design principles (Typography, Color theory, Layout, Visual Hierarchy, Gestalt laws).
Phase 2: Figma mastery (Auto Layout, Components, Variants, Interactive Prototyping).
Phase 3: UX Research (User personas, Journey mapping, Usability testing, Information architecture).
Phase 4: Design Systems, Micro-interactions, Accessibility guidelines, Portfolio creation.

Blockchain Developer.title: Blockchain Developer
Blockchain Developer.description: Architects decentralized applications (dApps), smart contracts, and cryptographic ledger protocols ensuring verifiable trust and security.
interview_tips: Demonstrate thorough knowledge of smart contract security vulnerabilities (Reentrancy, Integer Overflow, Front-running).
Understand EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) mechanics, gas optimization, and storage slots.
Build and deploy audited smart contracts on testnets (Sepolia/Polygon).
interview_questions: What is a Reentrancy attack in Solidity and how do you protect against it using Checks-Effects-Interactions?
Explain the differences between Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS) consensus.
How do you optimize smart contracts to minimize gas costs for end users?
What are ERC-20, ERC-721, and ERC-1155 standards and their use cases?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Cryptography basics (Public-Private keys, Hashing, Merkle Trees), Blockchain architecture.
Phase 2: Solidity programming, Smart Contract lifecycle, EVM fundamentals.
Phase 3: Development frameworks (Hardhat/Foundry), Ethers.js integration with React frontend.
Phase 4: Smart contract security auditing, DeFi protocols, Layer 2 rollups (Arbitrum, Optimism).

Embedded Systems & IoT Engineer.title: Embedded Systems & IoT Engineer
Embedded Systems & IoT Engineer.description: Develops low-level firmware, device drivers, and connected Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems interfacing software with physical microcontrollers and sensors.
interview_tips: Master pointer manipulation, bitwise operations, memory-mapped I/O, and volatile keyword in C.
Explain real-time operating systems concepts (task scheduling, semaphores, mutexes, priority inversion).
Be prepared to read hardware schematics and explain protocol timing diagrams.
interview_questions: What does the 'volatile' keyword signify in C and why is it essential for embedded hardware registers?
Explain Priority Inversion in RTOS and how Priority Inheritance resolves it.
Compare I2C vs SPI in terms of speed, bus topology, pin count, and duplex capability.
How would you design a battery-powered IoT sensor to operate reliably for 5+ years?
learning_roadmap: Phase 1: Advanced C programming (pointers, bit manipulation, memory management), digital electronics.
Phase 2: Microcontroller architecture (ARM Cortex / ESP32), GPIO, Timers, ADC, Interrupt handling.
Phase 3: Serial protocols (UART, SPI, I2C, CAN), RTOS concepts with FreeRTOS.
Phase 4: IoT connectivity (Wi-Fi, BLE, MQTT, HTTP), low-power optimization, Embedded Linux.
